explanation: The hypothesis is a literature-supported alternative for strength in some complex concentrated alloys: E1, E2, and E5 directly support spatial fault-energy fluctuations, hard local motifs, and rugged dislocation-energy landscapes. However, it is not a reconstruction of the hidden study. The target concerns homogenized equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals and separates three regimes: MSAD-controlled solid-solution resistance, phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling below roughly 60–77 K, and Mn/Fe-associated Portevin–Le Chatelier pinning at elevated temperature. The generated response instead generalizes across FCC and BCC alloys, uses conventional low-entropy alloys as an uncontrolled baseline, and predicts only a vague increase in strength with chemical fluctuations. E3 and E4 are tangential, and none of the cited evidence establishes the proposed entropy-to-fluctuation relationship or the claimed broad boundary. A useful test would hold crystal structure, orientation, grain structure, temperature, and average fault energy approximately fixed while varying measured fault-energy variance, then compare CRSS and dislocation morphology against MSAD or elastic-misfit predictions.
